The subprogramme provides short-term paid employment opportunities to Palestine refugees residing in camps across UNRWA fields of operation (excluding Gaza), through the construction, rehabilitation and maintenance of essential infrastructure, notably schools, health centres and water and sanitation networks. As well as constituting an important source of income, these opportunities serve to develop the skills and long-term employability prospects of some of the most vulnerable Palestine refugees.

subprogrammes.name: Palestine refugees are accurately registered and their status is securely maintained

objectives: 26.96 The objective, to which this subprogramme contributes, is to ensure that Palestine refugees are accurately registered and their status is securely maintained.

performance.title: Historic family records are preserved and secured through large-scale digitization
performance.narrative:
26.99 Historic family files, comprising nearly 30 million documents, constitute the core evidentiary basis for establishing the registration status, lineage and entitlements of Palestine refugees across generations. Many of these records, held in paper form for decades, remain vulnerable to deterioration, damage and loss, particularly in contexts affected by conflict and displacement. In 2023, UNRWA initiated a project aimed at ensuring the digital preservation and accessibility of historic family files for Palestine refugees, stored in a data centre established in Luxembourg. During 2024 and 2025, the subprogramme accelerated the digitization of historic family files, including the scanning, review and classification of archival records into secure digital formats. This work strengthened the protection and integrity of irreplaceable documentation, improved the reliability of registration data and established a structured digital archive to support verification processes and future analytical use.
26.100 Progress towards the objective is presented in the performance measure below (see table 26.11).

measures.label: Table 26.11
measures.value: Expanded access to secure and preserved registration records for Palestine refugees, with the digitization of approximately 10 million historical documents, strengthening the integrity of identity verification and the continuity of services

planned.title: Registered Palestine refugees have improved digital access to their records and services
planned.narrative:
26.101 Registration with UNRWA serves to verify identity and establish eligibility for access by Palestine refugees to Agency-provided services. Maintaining accurate, up-to-date registration records is essential to minimize risks of fraud, safeguard services to those eligible and inform the Agency’s strategic planning and decision-making. The subprogramme supports the transition from paper-based, in-person registration to digital registration through the eUNRWA platform. Launched in 2023, eUNRWA enables registered individuals to securely access their individual and family registration records, submit and track requests to update life-event information, and download their Family Registration eCard remotely. The system enhances accessibility for Palestine refugees, including those temporarily or permanently outside UNRWA fields of operation, while strengthening the accuracy and timeliness of registration data.
Lessons learned and planned change
26.102 The lesson for the subprogramme is that requiring in-person registration creates a structural barrier to maintaining accurate records in contexts of displacement, movement restrictions and insecurity, resulting in delays, incomplete updates and uneven workloads across offices. The introduction of eUNRWA showed that enabling remote access, combined with centralized processing of requests, significantly improves timeliness, reduces backlogs and ensures more consistent service delivery. In applying the lesson, the subprogramme will focus on enhancing system functionality and workflow management to handle increasing volumes and more complex transactions, while sustaining high levels of digital usage and data accuracy.
26.103 Expected progress towards the objective is presented in the performance measure below (see figure 26.XXII).

overview.name: Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for the Middle East Peace Process
objectives: 3.II.2 The objective, to which the Office contributes, is to achieve a comprehensive, just and lasting resolution to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict based on the two-State solution and to improve the socioeconomic conditions of the Palestinian people.

performance.title: Evidence-based recovery planning for Gaza
performance.narrative:
3.II.13 In 2025, the Office continued its good offices and programmatic efforts to support preparation and planning for the future of Gaza, in order to improve Palestinian lives, rights and dignity, ensure security for Israelis and Palestinians and advance the two-State solution. Since late 2023, the World Bank, the European Union and the United Nations have been working collectively on damage and needs assessments. In 2025, an interim rapid damage and needs assessment was conducted, which provided a comprehensive analysis of the damage, losses and needs related to the conflict in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem. The findings provide a valuable evidence base to inform stakeholders of the impact in Gaza and the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, on the population, economy, physical assets, infrastructure and service delivery, as well as to conduct an estimate of the needs for physical infrastructure reconstruction, economic and social recovery, and service restoration in selected sectors. Following the ceasefire agreement in October 2025, the Office supported efforts of the United Nations and its humanitarian partners to implement a 60-day response plan to meet the humanitarian needs of Palestinians in Gaza, including through political engagement with key stakeholders to facilitate access, movement and other enabling conditions, as well as engagement with Member States to support resource mobilization and advocacy efforts.
3.II.14 Progress towards the objective is presented in the performance measure below (see table 3.II.1).

entities.name: Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon
priorities: Maintenance of international peace and security

overview.name: Office of the United Nations Special Coordinator for Lebanon
objectives: The objective, to which this mission contributes, is to prevent and mitigate conflict between Israel and Lebanon and work towards an eventual permanent ceasefire and to extend and consolidate State authority in support of the territorial integrity, sovereignty and political independence of Lebanon.

performance.title: Consolidation of the cessation of hostilities
performance.narrative:
In 2025, the Special Coordinator exercised her good offices with relevant stakeholders in Lebanon, Israel, the region and beyond, to promote confidence-building measures to consolidate the cessation of hostilities arrangement of November 2024 to promote enduring security and stability for communities on both sides of the Blue Line. Through public and closed-door channels, the Special Coordinator urged all parties to leverage the momentum provided by the cessation of hostilities arrangement to take concrete steps towards negotiated solutions to advance long-stalled provisions of Security Council resolution 1701 (2006), including through, inter alia, promoting and supporting the commencement of a civilian dialogue track.
The Special Coordinator also offered her good offices to support the Government of Lebanon in its effort to establish exclusive State control over weapons, including through mobilization of international support for the Lebanese Armed Forces (LAF) to ensure a strengthened presence and effective deployment south of the Litani River as a critical first step, while continuing work towards the full extension of State authority across all of Lebanon’s territory.

planned.narrative:
In 2025, the mission supported political and diplomatic efforts and regularly engaged with the parties to address outstanding provisions of resolution 1701 (2006) and consolidate the 2024 cessation of hostilities arrangement towards creating the space for progress on longer-term objectives, such as the restoration of Lebanon’s territorial integrity, including through the withdrawal of the Israel Defense Forces from north of the Blue Line, and resolution of disputed border areas. The resolution of disputed border areas witnessed some renewed interest without meeting the planned target for 2025. Meanwhile, building on conducive openings with Syria, the mission supported the nascent exploration of border delineation initiatives between the two countries.
For 2027, the mission will employ its good offices to support the restoration and consolidation of a cessation of hostilities, including through leveraging the momentum for dialogue between the parties to reach negotiated solutions on outstanding provisions of resolution 1701 (2006), including the disarmament of non-State armed groups, the withdrawal of Israeli forces from north of the Blue Line, and a border dispute resolution as potentially significant aspects of a long-term solution. In parallel, the mission will leverage windows of opportunity, in cooperation with relevant stakeholders, to facilitate progress towards a border delineation track between Lebanon and Syria.

planned.label: Result 2
planned.title: extension and consolidation of State authority and strengthened governance to advance Lebanon’s stability and recovery
planned.narrative:
For 2027, the mission will build on Lebanon’s Government decisions to achieve the nationwide state monopoly on arms. Noting potential gaps following the end of UNIFIL’s operations on 31 December 2026, UNSCOL will continue to lead UN efforts to mobilize international assistance to empower Lebanon’s security institutions and to advance progress towards a national security strategy and related architecture. In support of Lebanon’s overall stability and recovery, the mission will advocate for the effective and uninterrupted functioning of governance institutions and for tangible progress in the reform and macroeconomic stabilization track.
The lesson for the mission was that consolidating the cessation of hostilities was not insulated from the volatile international and regional context, which impacted the calculations of all parties and ultimately led to the collapse of the cessation of hostilities arrangement. The mission will, therefore, continue to exercise its good offices with stakeholders in the region and beyond to shield progress from externalities. The growth of cross-cutting and interconnected challenges facing Lebanon, which span the humanitarian, development, political and security fields, have reinforced the need for the deeper integration between related pillars of the UN’s work, which UNSCOL will be prioritizing in its working methods, communication products, planning and assessments, among other streams of work.

entities.name: United Nations Support Mission in Libya
priorities: Maintenance of international peace and security

overview.name: United Nations Support Mission in Libya
objectives: The objective, to which this Mission contributes, is to support an inclusive Libyan-led political process and rights-based national reconciliation, conflict prevention and peacebuilding efforts; strengthen rule of law institutions, transitional justice processes and State-building efforts to optimize readiness for planning and implementing credible, transparent and inclusive elections; advance human rights, gender equality and women’s and youth political participation; support the reform of the security sector, disarmament, demobilization and reintegration efforts and the further implementation of the October 2020 ceasefire agreement.

performance.title: Strengthened rule of law institutions and transitional justice process protecting the rights of all people in Libya
performance.narrative:
In 2025, UNSMIL supported concrete steps to strengthen rule of law institutions and advance transitional justice through national-level accountability engagement, reviews of the legal framework and capacity-building for justice and security actors. As a result, national and local authorities, judicial institutions and representatives of victims convened to accelerate execution of national and international arrest warrants linked to the Tarhuna mass graves, enhance cooperation on extradition requests and support the resumption of excavations to identify missing persons. Stakeholders from Murzuq also convened in 2025 to address enforced disappearances and gross violations committed between 2019 and 2023. In addition, a joint committee, consisting of Libyan authorities, UNSMIL, UN agencies and other local technical parties, reviewed a preliminary draft law on missing persons to strengthen the legal basis for investigations, documentation and redress.
The Mission also organized specialised sessions for judges, prosecutors, investigators, prison staff and security actors covered international human rights and humanitarian law, international detention standards and related international processes. In addition, civil society reporting capacity was strengthened through structured engagement with international human rights mechanisms. This included the facilitation of civil society engagement with the Universal Periodic Review mechanism of the United Nations Human Rights Council, including through thematic civil society submissions. These actions improved the evidence base, legal readiness and institutional coordination needed for future accountability and victim-centred transitional justice pathways.

planned.label: Result 2
planned.title: a comprehensive road map for holding national elections, towards the establishment of unified, elected, legitimate, inclusive and functional government institutions contributing to political stability and reconciliation
planned.narrative:
In 2025, UNSMIL delivered facilitation and good offices with key Libyan stakeholders to advance consensus on pathways toward elections and institutional unity. It established an Advisory Committee of Libyan experts to provide options to overcome electoral obstacles which later informed the launch of the Structured Dialogue (SD) in December 2025, aimed at addressing impediments to elections and underlying conflict drivers. In parallel, UNSMIL engaged political actors, including the House of Representatives and the High Council of State on reconstituting the High National Elections Commission (HNEC) and finalizing the electoral legal framework.
In 2027, UNSMIL will pursue an integrated political approach to advance a viable electoral roadmap and institutional unity. It will consolidate SD outcomes to support consensus on the electoral political framework and continue good offices to bridge divisions and enable a unified government through elections. UNSMIL will continue to engage all parties on human rights and rule of law issues as an integral part of the Libyan-led and Libyan-owned political process. It will prioritize addressing arbitrary arrest and detention, the protection of civic space and civil society engagement as key enablers of the political and electoral processes.

planned.title: economic governance and political economy drivers of conflict are addressed in support of the political process
planned.narrative:
In 2027, UNSMIL will advance the economic track as a core pillar of the political process integrating political economy analysis into mediation, negotiations and good offices to ensure that economic considerations directly inform engagement with political and security actors. It aims to realign incentives in support of institutional unity, reduce obstruction to reforms and create conditions conducive to credible national elections.
A key lesson is that impact depends on tighter integration of economic incentive analysis across political, security and economic tracks. Stand-alone or purely economic initiatives had limited effect when not linked to political incentives, security arrangements or coordinated international engagement. In applying the lesson, UNSMIL will adopt a more integrated and targeted approach, prioritize reducing economic drivers of conflict by working with sovereign state institutions to curb rent-seeking incentives, addressing sources of patronage, and promoting transparent and accountable and rules-based economic decision-making consistent with human rights principles.

performance.title: Sustained national and community commitment to the implementation of the Final Agreement as the path to lasting peace
performance.narrative:
In 2025, Colombian institutions, former combatants, communities as well as international partners reaffirmed their commitment to the Final Agreement, as the country’s roadmap to lasting peace. The Mission operated under tight financial constraints, closing nine local offices amid renewed violent clashes, politically motivated violence, and uneven progress in peace dialogues, all of which significantly impacted the environment conducive to the implementation of the Final Agreement. In this context, the Mission’s monitoring and verification of the Final Agreement remained instrumental in sustaining peace dividends and confidence in the process. Through technical advice, advocacy, engagement and good office efforts, the Mission supported key peacebuilding achievements in advancing processes for economic reintegration, land acquisition, contributing to preventing former combatants’ return to violence.
Prior to the mandate renewal in October 2025, the Mission continued its engagement with relevant entities, including through its participation in the Monitoring and Verification Mechanism (MVM) and by enhancing information-sharing mechanisms across the transitional justice system. These efforts contributed to the operationalization of the MVM and helped reinforce coordination among institutions responsible for implementing transitional justice measures.
The mandate pertaining to the monitoring of restorative sentences has been discontinued, after which all related verification activities have ceased.

planned.label: Result 1
planned.title: strengthened security conditions for communities in conflict-affected areas through advances in the implementation of the Final Agreement
planned.narrative:
In 2025, the Mission contributed to the adoption of key public policies and helped strengthen coordination mechanisms in view of consolidating institutional frameworks for prevention and protection measures benefitting former combatants, social leaders and communities. Given the evolving security situation in Colombia, the Mission continued its analysis of conflict dynamics across the country.
In 2027, the Mission will continue to advocate for advances in the institutional architecture and Government responses to strengthen effective security guarantees. The Mission will encourage coherent approaches between prevention, protection and actions to dismantle illegal organizations, aimed at improving security conditions in conflict-affected areas.

planned.narrative:
In 2025, the Mission contributed to strengthen reintegration public policies, supported and accompanied efforts in land delivery for groups of former combatants and promoted their economic sustainability. The Mission also engaged with relevant stakeholders to ensure judicial guarantees for former combatants.
In 2027, the Mission will continue to engage with relevant counterparts to advance the institutional framework and public policies for reintegration, ensuring the meaningful participation of former combatants. It will further encourage actions towards the sustainability of livelihood projects, access to employment and social services, as well as access to land and housing for the consolidation of the reintegration process of former combatants.

planned.label: Result 3
planned.title: strengthened foundations for the implementation of the comprehensive rural reform to rural communities
planned.narrative:
In 2027, the Mission will support the advancement of a comprehensive rural reform, including land access and formalization by the government, as well as the delivery of peace dividends to rural communities through territorial development projects. These efforts are key to bridge the gaps between rural and urban communities and set the foundations for sustainable peace.
The lesson for the Mission was that consistent and reliable land-related data would significantly enhance its ability to verify implementation of the comprehensive rural reform. Therefore, the Mission partially automated its data collection tools for precision and consistency of its verification inputs, enabling improved analytical quality to its work. In applying this new tool, the Mission will enhance its verification’s capacities for the effective verification and monitoring of the implementation of comprehensive rural reform.

entities.name: United Nations Youth Office
priorities: Promotion of sustained economic growth and sustainable development

overview.name: United Nations Youth Office
objectives: The objective, to which the Office contributes, is to ensure the meaningful engagement and leadership of young people in the work of the United Nations and accelerated action at the global, regional and country levels to empower young people, promote their rights and address their needs.

performance.title: Progress in advancing youth priorities and meaningful youth engagement
performance.narrative:
In 2025, the UN Youth Office, through its flagship initiative, the UN Youth Compass — notably the global #YouthLead Festival and decentralized Dialogues — significantly expanded the scale and reach of youth engagement in global processes. The initiative engaged over 75,000 young people from 182 countries, enabling them to contribute to forward-looking policy discussions and elevating youth priorities across key global platforms. These contributions supported the integration of youth priorities into United Nations processes, including the launch of Youth2030 Phase 2 (2025–2030), which introduced strengthened accountability for meaningful youth engagement, with 67 per cent of performance areas rated “green” across UN Country Teams. They also informed the advancement of global principles for meaningful, inclusive and safe youth engagement under the Pact for the Future. Through these efforts, more structured and accountable approaches to youth engagement were strengthened, enabling young people to contribute to shaping global policy and sustainable development.
Progress towards the objective is presented in the performance measure below (see table 1.163).

measures.value: Youth priorities integrated into United Nations processes, with more structured and accountable approaches to meaningful youth engagement established

planned.label: Result 3
planned.title: Strengthened youth participation in peace and security processes
planned.narrative: In line with Action 20 of the Pact for the Future, Member States committed to accelerating implementation of the Youth, Peace and Security agenda and recognized that the full, effective, safe, and meaningful participation of youth is critical to maintaining and promoting international peace and security. Efforts across the United Nations system have focused on shifting from symbolic inclusion of youth to more structured and influential youth engagement in peace and security processes. In 2025, the Office demonstrated that purposeful convening and advocacy efforts - including through the #YouthLead Festival and decentralized Dialogues held in September 2025 - can mobilize youth engagement at scale and translate political commitments into emerging standards and tools.
